question.text: When an investor uses derivatives to protect an existing portfolio from adverse price movements, this is known as:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 210, hedging is the use of derivatives to protect an open position in the underlying from the risks of future price movements. Pages 210-211 contrast this with speculation (a directional view without an underlying position) and arbitrage (exploiting price differentials). The Trap: Speculation takes a derivative position without an underlying position. Arbitrage exploits price differentials between markets. Market making is a separate role and is not the source-supported label for protecting an existing portfolio. Note: Hedging is identified specifically by the existence of an open underlying position whose risk the derivative is intended to offset.
